oneLiner: A pure-play NAND flash maker earning record margins on AI storage demand, priced as if those earnings are about to collapse. The market is betting this is an ordinary memory peak; management is betting multi-year contracts have changed the cycle. The stock works if earnings merely plateau.
thesis: Data center is now the engine. Datacenter was ~44% of Q1 FY27 revenue against 12% a year earlier, and management expects data center bit demand to grow about 40% in calendar 2027, so the mix keeps moving toward the least price-sensitive buyer.

Contracts cover a rising share of bits. About half of FY2027 bits and two-thirds of FY2028 bits are committed under multi-year agreements with price floors, 95% of them with investment-grade customers; two more were signed in the quarter.
The price already assumes a bust. The reverse DCF needs forward earnings to fall about 21% a year for seven years, so the stock does not need growth, only a decline slower than that.
Cash return is large against the share count. Management plans to return 100% of excess cash; one quarter of adjusted free cash flow retired about 2% of the shares even at prices far above today's.

latestQuarter.label: Q1 FY2027 (ended Oct 2, 2026; reported Oct 29, 2026)
points: Revenue $11.03B, +23% QoQ and +378% YoY (consensus ~$10.7B); sequential growth about 60% volume, 40% pricing.
Gross margin 85.0% GAAP, 85.1% non-GAAP; non-GAAP operating margin 80.4% on $513M of operating expenses.
GAAP diluted EPS $52.60 (net income $8.10B); non-GAAP EPS $49.51 vs consensus $46.67. Per-share figures are pre-split.
End markets: Datacenter $4,802M (+61% QoQ), Edge $5,832M (+7% QoQ, below the ~$6.1B expected), Consumer $397M (-29% QoQ).
Operating cash flow $6.36B, adjusted free cash flow $5.70B; $5.0B of buybacks (~3.2M shares); cash $5.1B, no debt.
8-for-1 stock split: shares distributed after the close on Nov 19, 2026; split-adjusted trading from Nov 20.

latestProse: Q1 FY2027 (ended Oct 2, 2026; reported Oct 29) beat on every headline: revenue $11.03B (+23% QoQ, +378% YoY) against ~$10.7B expected, non-GAAP gross margin 85.1% and non-GAAP EPS $49.51 against $46.67. Datacenter grew 61% sequentially to $4.80B. The stock still fell more than 13% in the days after, for three reasons. First, the mix of growth changed: about 60% of the sequential gain was volume and 40% price, where the prior quarter was two-thirds price. Second, everything outside the data center slowed: Edge rose only 7% to $5.83B, short of the ~$6.1B expected, and Consumer fell 29% as buyers balked at higher prices. Third, JV partner Kioxia said on Oct 30 that its price gains slowed to the mid-20% range from about 70%. A sector rout followed on Nov 5 (the stock fell 22% in a day) after Qualcomm blamed weak handset sales on memory costs and the Nov 3 midterm results raised fears of tighter data-center permitting; on Nov 10 Counterpoint data showed Sandisk's NAND share slipping to 11% in Q2 2026 from 13%.
guidanceProse: Q2 FY2027 guide: revenue $12.2-12.6B (+11% to +14% QoQ, after quarters of +51% and +23%), non-GAAP gross margin 84.5-85.5%, non-GAAP operating expenses $540-560M, tax rate 14.3% and non-GAAP EPS $55-57 on ~151M diluted shares (pre-split; $6.88-7.13 on the post-split count). So margins are guided flat at the peak while growth decelerates - the guide neither confirms nor refutes the cycle call. On the call management kept its bit-growth plan at mid-to-high teens, said the contract pipeline exceeds available supply through the end of the decade, and guided FY2027 capex up to a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue. The CEO said the company is 'executing on the strategy that we outlined at Investor Day' (Aug 13: mid-to-high-teens revenue growth at ~80% gross margin for 2028-2030).
segments: Datacenter (enterprise SSD / AI storage): $4,802M in Q1 FY27, ~44% of revenue, +61% QoQ; was $269M a year earlier.
Edge (client, mobile, OEM): $5,832M, ~53% of revenue, +7% QoQ, +320% YoY; low-end PC and phone units under pressure.
Consumer (retail cards and drives): $397M, ~4% of revenue, -29% QoQ, -39% YoY as retail adjusts to higher prices.
competitive: Counterpoint Q2 CY2026 NAND share: Samsung 25%, SK Hynix 22%, YMTC 14% (top three for the first time); Sandisk slipped to 11% from 13% in Q1, sixth by volume.
Kioxia is both JV partner (shared fabs at Yokkaichi and Kitakami, common BiCS roadmap, JV extended to 2034) and a direct rival in enterprise SSD.
Samsung and SK Hynix have prioritised HBM and DRAM capex, a key reason NAND supply stayed tight; their appetite to add NAND capacity is the biggest swing factor.
YMTC's volume gains are the wildcard supply threat, limited for now by a low enterprise SSD share and export controls.
moat: NAND is a commodity: no supplier has held pricing power through a full cycle, and an 85% gross margin is cycle rent, not moat. The durable edges are cost and scale through the Kioxia JV and the BiCS8 / BiCS10 node roadmap, plus - if they hold in a downturn - multi-year contracts that turn spot exposure into committed volume at floor prices. Those contracts have never been through a falling-price market.
risks: Peak margins. No NAND maker has sustained 80%+ gross margin through a cycle, and price is already contributing less of the growth; the base case assumes margin slips to the high 70s, the bear case to the high 50s.

Demand destruction outside the data center. Edge and Consumer are still 56% of revenue; Edge missed expectations, Consumer is shrinking, and TrendForce reports wafer prices at highs that retail channels cannot absorb.

Capex is understated in the filings. Purchases of property were only $54M (0.5% of revenue) because fab spending runs through the Kioxia JV: management's gross capex was $378M, loans to and investments in the JV rose to $827M from $678M, and the partners plan over $31B in Japan through 2032.

Buybacks near the top and a rising diluted count. The $5.0B spent in Q1 bought ~3.2M shares at roughly $1,560 each, well above where the stock trades now; average diluted shares are still up 3.4% YoY (149M to 154M) on stock compensation, though shares outstanding fell to 144M from 146M in the quarter.

Earnings quality and receivables. GAAP net income ($8.10B) exceeded non-GAAP ($7.62B) on roughly $0.5B of non-operating gains, the tax rate is only ~14%, and receivables rose 40% QoQ to $6.6B against 23% revenue growth.
catalysts: Nov 19-20, 2026: 8-for-1 split takes effect; per-share figures in this note need dividing by 8 once the price feed is split-adjusted.
Mid-Dec 2026: Micron fiscal Q1 report - NAND pricing and 2027 supply commentary (debate 2); date unverified.
Late Dec 2026: TrendForce 1Q27 NAND contract price forecast (debates 1 and 2).
Late Jan 2027: Q2 FY2027 report - gross margin, Edge trend, contract coverage (debates 1 and 3); Samsung and SK Hynix Q4 calls with 2027 NAND capex (debate 2).

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings, as for other memory names: the reverse DCF quantifies the annual earnings decline the market implies, to set against management's 2028-2030 growth targets. Only 3 years of standalone filings exist (Feb 2025 spin).

verdict.summary: The business has kept improving since August while the stock has roughly halved, so the question is no longer whether results are good but how fast they fade. The price discounts an earnings decline of about a fifth a year for seven years; our base case, in which FY2028 earnings merely hold near the FY2027 run-rate, is worth about a third more, and the bear case - contract floors bend and earnings halve - loses about 40%. That skew is favourable but the bear case is a normal memory outcome, not a tail, so size it accordingly. Two things would change the view: gross margin guided below 80% while contracts are supposedly holding it there, and evidence that Samsung, SK Hynix or YMTC are adding NAND supply faster than demand in 2027.
wtb: FY2028 non-GAAP EPS stays above ~$200 pre-split (~$25 post-split), within about 12% of the ~$228 FY2027 run-rate, rather than halving.
Non-GAAP gross margin holds above 75% through calendar 2027 as contract price floors are tested by falling spot prices.
Datacenter passes 50% of revenue by Q4 FY2027 (June 2027 quarter) and grows fast enough to offset flat-to-down Edge and Consumer.
Industry NAND bit supply grows no faster than demand in calendar 2027 (roughly low-20s percent).

bear.why: Supply responds and phone, PC and retail buyers keep cutting; spot prices fall hard in 2027 and contract floors are renegotiated rather than enforced. Revenue drops about a third from FY2027's ~$50B, gross margin falls to the high 50s and EPS more than halves. The market pays 5x falling earnings. A full historical bust (30-40% gross margin) sits below this case.

base.why: Bits grow mid-to-high teens, prices ease low-teens from the peak and contract floors mostly hold; revenue is roughly flat on the FY2027 exit rate with gross margin ~78% and net margin ~61%. Buybacks offset the lower margin, so EPS holds near the FY2027 level. Earnings that plateau instead of collapsing still earn only a deep-cyclical 5x.

bull.why: AI storage keeps NAND undersupplied into 2028; revenue grows ~23%, ahead of the investor-day mid-to-high-teens target, at an ~84% gross margin and ~67% net margin. With two-thirds of bits contracted and FY2029 visibly up, the market starts to treat the earnings as durable and pays 7x.

scenarioModel.note: All per-share figures are PRE-SPLIT, matching the price in the data feed as of Nov 14, 2026. The 8-for-1 split trades from Nov 20, 2026: when the feed switches to split-adjusted prices, divide every scenario EPS by 8 (bear ~$13.3, base ~$29.4, bull ~$38.5) and use ~1,080M shares. FY2027 base year: Q1 $11.0B + Q2 guide $12.4B + ~$13.2B + ~$13.8B = ~$50B revenue and ~$228 non-GAAP EPS. EPS = revenue x net margin / ~135M average diluted shares in FY2028 (151M guided for Q2 FY27, less continued buybacks): bear $34B x 42%, base $52B x 61%, bull $62B x 67%. EPS is non-GAAP (excludes stock compensation and non-operating gains). Multiples are applied to FY2028 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Do the contract price floors hold when spot prices fall?
debates.bull: Half of FY2027 bits and two-thirds of FY2028 bits are committed, 95% with investment-grade buyers that together generate ~$130B of operating cash flow; management says the floors keep gross margin near 80% and the pipeline exceeds supply through 2030. Minimum contract value is roughly $90B (sources range $88.9-93.9B; current figure unverified).
debates.bear: Floors and ceilings are undisclosed, the contracts were signed at shortage prices, and in every prior downturn large buyers reopened terms. Customer prepayments received fell to $465M in Q1 from $1.94B in Q4, so new commitments carry less cash up front.
debates.view: This is the debate that separates base from bear. We assume the floors bend but do not break: margin in the high 70s, not the mid 80s and not the 50s. A guide below 80% while spot prices are still rising would mean the floors are lower than claimed, and we would move weight to the bear case.

signpost.metric: Non-GAAP gross margin guide for Q3 FY2027 and share of FY2028 bits contracted
signpost.threshold: bearish if margin guided below 82% or FY2028 coverage stalls at two-thirds; bullish if coverage reaches 75%+

debates.q: Is the supply response coming in 2027?
debates.bull: Sandisk is holding bit growth to mid-to-high teens, new fab capacity (Kitakami Fab3) is not due before fiscal 2029, and Citi reportedly expects 2027 memory production up 22% against demand up 26% (press summary, unverified). SK Hynix said on Oct 28 it sees demand ahead of supply through 2030.
debates.bear: An 85% gross margin is the strongest possible invitation to add wafers. Kioxia's price gains have already slowed to the mid-20% range, YMTC holds 14% share, and Sandisk's own spending is larger than its filings show because it runs through the JV.
debates.view: Supply is the slower of the two risks: fab lead times protect calendar 2027, less so 2028. That is why the scenarios are struck on FY2028. We stay positive while announced industry bit growth stays below ~20%.

signpost.metric: Calendar 2027 NAND bit supply growth guided by Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia and Micron; TrendForce 1Q27 contract price forecast
signpost.threshold: bearish if any of the top three guides NAND bit growth above 25% or 1Q27 contract prices are forecast flat or down

debates.q: Can the data center carry the company while Edge and Consumer stall?
debates.bull: Datacenter added $1.8B of revenue in one quarter and is on track to be the majority of sales within a few quarters; data center is roughly half of industry NAND bits, up from about 20% early in the decade.
debates.bear: High prices are destroying demand at the low end: Qualcomm's handset chip revenue fell 26% and it blamed memory costs, and the midterm results raised the risk of data-center permitting delays (UBS: ~30% of 2028 capacity at risk) just as Sandisk becomes dependent on that one buyer group.
debates.view: Mix shift is real and in the base case; what is not in it is a sequential decline in Edge. One flat Edge quarter is noise, a falling one means price increases have hit their ceiling.

signpost.metric: Edge revenue QoQ and Datacenter share of revenue in Q2 FY2027
signpost.threshold: bearish if Edge falls QoQ below ~$5.8B; bullish if Datacenter exceeds 48% of revenue

changelog.change: Rebuilt as a v3 decision note after Q1 FY2027 (revenue $11.0B, non-GAAP GM 85.1%, Q2 guide $12.2-12.6B, 8-for-1 split). Scenario values on FY2028 EPS, pre-split: bear $530 / base $1,175 / bull $2,156. View moved from balanced-to-sceptical to Positive - sized for a cycle: results improved while the stock roughly halved from the post-investor-day level.

Q4 FY2026 beat and Aug 13 investor day (2028-2030 targets of mid-to-high-teens growth at ~80% gross margin). View: balanced, sceptical that a 30% rally should pay for the claim that the NAND cycle is over.
